free_tier.stated: No storage quota of its own. It is a serving and permanence layer over npm and GitHub, so the quota is whatever the origin package holds. Hard limits: packages >150 MB and (for GitHub) single files >20 MB are refused by default, raisable on request.

retention.stated: | Retention is stronger than the origin: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion

record.tooling: Plain GET on cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/<pkg>@<ver>/<path> and /gh/<owner>/<repo>@<ref>/<path>. No client needed. Cache-purge API exists (email-gated).
record.chaining: Chains onto npm packages or GitHub repositories: assets published to npm or GitHub releases can be served via jsDelivr edge URLs with 1-year immutable caching and unmetered egress.
record.limits_note: 150 MB per npm package, 20 MB per single GitHub file (both default, raisable via GitHub issue). Rate limiting applies to purge, not to reads. Enforcement is the technical risk, not the capability.
record.reliability_note: Retention is stronger than the origin: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion. We do not accept removal requests simply because a package or version was unpublished, deleted upstream, or is no longer needed.' Once a URL has been fetched it keeps working after you delete the npm package. That is a genuine cold-archive property. Counter-risk: a 150 MB package cap means a naive >150 MB npm tarball 403s ('Package size exceeded the configured limit of 150 MB') even though npm itself accepted it.

evidence.proved: 'no bandwidth limits or premium features and its completely free to use by anybody'
'no limits on bandwidth or number of requests'; 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion'
(README) — 'Packages larger than 150 MB or single files larger than 20 MB (in the case of GitHub) are not supported by default'
probe: GET -> 200, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable, Server: cloudflare
probe: GET -> 403, body 'Package size exceeded the configured limit of 150 MB.' (confirms the cap is real and enforced at fetch time)

record.notes: No storage quota of its own. It is a serving and permanence layer over npm and GitHub, so the quota is whatever the origin package holds. Hard limits: packages >150 MB and (for GitHub) single files >20 MB are refused by default, raisable on request.

record.provider: jsDelivr as the free CDN layer over GitHub repos

free_tier.stated: free with no limits on bandwidth or number of requests; GitHub-proxy soft limits of 10 000 actively accessed files and 100 000 files per repository
free_tier.notes: the file-count soft limits are not automatically enforced

per_object_cap.stated: files up to 20 MB through the GitHub proxy, regardless of repository size

retention.stated: | Immutable: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion'. Deletion upstream does not remove it from jsDelivr.

egress.terms: Unmetered and cached at edge locations with headers 'Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable' and Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *.

record.tooling: URL pattern https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/USER/REPO@TAG/path. No client needed, no auth, no config. Purge API exists for cache busting.
record.chaining: Serving layer only: pair it with Releases (storage) or a git repo (small files). One repo backs 1 TiB/day because the edge absorbs repeats with a 1-year immutable TTL.
record.limits_note: Git repo files only — release assets are NOT served (probed: /gh/cli/cli@v2.102.1/dist/README.md -> 404). ~20 MB effective per-file ceiling for the GitHub proxy (the git-unlimited-storage README states 'jsDelivr per file | 20 MB'); hard per-file/per-package caps are undocumented and enforced at request time. Does not serve the >2 GiB release assets, so the serving path for big objects stays on GitHub's own Fastly edge.
record.reliability_note: Immutable: 'Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion'. Deletion upstream does not remove it from jsDelivr. Extension blocklist exists; binaries with unusual extensions can be refused.

evidence.proved: 'there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests'; soft limit '100 000' files per repository
probe: GET cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/jquery/jquery@3.7.1/dist/jquery.min.js -> 200, Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, s-maxage=31536000, immutable, Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *
jsDelivr CDN sets no limit on bandwidth or on the number of requests

evidence.proved: the GitHub-proxy recommendation is at most 10 000 actively accessed files per repository
evidence.quote: We recommend that the number of actively accessed files per repository does not exceed 10 000.

evidence.proved: the GitHub-proxy soft limit is 100 000 files per repository
evidence.quote: The soft limit for the number of files per repository is 100 000.

evidence.proved: the soft limits are not automatically enforced
evidence.quote: These limits are not automatically enforced by us, but you agree not to exceed them.

evidence.proved: a jsDelivr member states the GitHub-proxy per-file limit of 20 MB
evidence.quote: We actually allow files up to 20 MB for GitHub regardless of the overall repo size

evidence.proved: served immutable files can outlive upstream deletion
evidence.quote: Previously served immutable files may be retained in permanent storage even after upstream deletion.

record.notes: Provides CDN distribution rather than origin storage. Documentation states 'there are no limits on bandwidth or number of requests' (the provider), with soft limits of 10,000 actively accessed files and 100,000 files per repository.
